kata.name: Visitor-as-sum-type near-floor control: two variants, both sampled by the conventional dispatch test
kata.series_report: docs/ref/ploeh-grounding.md §6 item 3 (proposed candidate); docs/DESIGN.md §4.4 (rule lens mapping)
kata.series_verdict: killed (pre-registered: at the 2-variant floor the sampled scripted dispatch test catches all 3 injected behavior-changing faults; the lens buys zero unique detections)

expected.detail: remove the `visit_lit` rule; kind=lit is uncovered -> underconstraint (hypothesized)
duplicate the `visit_lit` registration and declare `DeclaredDisjoint`; the lit input is shared -> violation (executed)
insert a broad (lit OR neg) registration before `visit_neg`; `visit_neg` is dead under PriorityOrder -> redundant (executed)

witness.question: which action applies? no rule covers this input class

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/visitor_sum_types_baseline.py --assert: the floor sample checks both variants (lit, neg) against the frozen actions. NF1 removes a sampled registration, NF2 makes the sampled lit dispatch ambiguous under DeclaredDisjoint, and NF3 changes the sampled neg action; all 3 floor faults are caught, so the lens's unique set is empty.

expressibility_gap.invariant: visitor method bodies compute the interpretation
expressibility_gap.why: the rule presentation's action is an opaque string; the lens proves every variant reaches a named action, never that the action's implementation returns the correct value

expressibility_gap.invariant: runtime class identity derived from state, not a declared `kind` column
expressibility_gap.why: X must be a finite product of typed attribute columns; identity computed from state is outside the declared attribute alphabet

expressibility_gap.invariant: double dispatch over (node kind x visitor type)
expressibility_gap.why: the rule presentation has one domain and one action function; two visitors are two documents with no cross-visitor consistency check

discrepancies: Floor scope: all three injected floor faults are behavior-changing. A behavior-preserving derivable handler cannot be expressed on two variants with distinct actions (a broad rule covering both variants and preserving both actions would need two actions), so the derivable class is above-floor only; the zero-unique result is scoped to behavior-changing faults.
procedure: 1. Declare the two-variant floor table (lit, neg) and bind both variants with --values kind=lit,neg; the lens reports zero findings.
2. Freeze the floor sampled scripted dispatch test over both variants before injecting faults.
3. Inject NF1 (remove lit), NF2 (duplicate lit + DeclaredDisjoint), NF3 (broad lit OR neg registration before neg).
4. Execute the baseline (--assert) and catherine rules on each variant; the sampled test names every injected fault.
5. Zero unique detections -> the control self-negates: verdict killed, no advantage at the floor.
